findings_qualitative.value: Salt emission is found where dust is optically thin; molecules other than NaCl originate primarily in the bipolar outflow, whose base corotates with the disk.

evidence.quote: All other molecules that we have mapped – H$_2$O, AlO, SiO, SiS, SO, and SO$_2$ – appear to originate primarily in the bipolar outflow.

claims.hypothesis: Dust opacity varies across the SrcI disk
claims.experiment: Spectral index maps from 43-340 GHz at 30 mas
claims.result: Spectral index ~2 in the midplane, ~3 at edges
claims.finding: Midplane optically thick, edges optically thin

evidence.quote: The continuum spectral index ranges from $\sim$2 along the midplane of the disk to $\sim$3 along the edges

claims.hypothesis: Salt traces the disk velocity field where dust is thin
claims.experiment: NaCl line maps compared with spectral index images
claims.result: NaCl lies in the surface layers with large spectral index gradient
claims.finding: NaCl is a tracer of the disk velocity field; rotational temperatures may be underestimated

evidence.quote: Salt emission is found in the dust layer at the surface of SrcI where there is a large spectral index gradient.

claims.hypothesis: Outflow chemistry is shaped by grain destruction and gas-phase reactions
claims.experiment: Maps of H2O, AlO, SiO, SiS, SO, SO2
claims.result: SiS filamentary at outflow edges; others in outflow
claims.finding: Si and Al released from grains form SiO and AlO; SiS forms via SO and SO2

evidence.quote: The molecular distributions suggest that Si and Al released from dust grains in the disk react with oxygen derived from H$_2$O to form SiO and AlO

limitations_admitted.value: SO and SO2 distributions are over-resolved; the U-line remains unidentified.

evidence.quote: The SO and distributions are over-resolved in these ALMA observations.
